findings.summary: Bind provider manifest and contract fetches to the installed HTTPS origin.
findings.failure_scenario: A manifest or separately fetched migration contract names an origin different from the installed provider channel.
findings.impact: Cross-origin provider intent could otherwise inherit installed-preauthorization trust.
findings.minimum_fix: Implemented exact normalized HTTPS-origin checks for installation manifests and event manifest or contract URLs, with persisted cross-origin negative fixtures and semantic tests.
findings.architecture_boundary: provider channel and non-executable change-intent intake

findings.summary: Enforce each persisted installation action ceiling without latent authority.
findings.failure_scenario: A lower action mode carries capabilities that its label does not authorize, including remote GitHub delivery below open_draft_pr.
findings.impact: A persisted installation could otherwise widen consumer-approved side effects.
findings.minimum_fix: Implemented mode-specific schema and semantic ceilings: notify_only grants no repository access or execution, scan_only remains read-only and external-route-free, and prepare_patch may use approved local patch authority but cannot carry GitHub branch, PR, or token issuance authority.
findings.architecture_boundary: Consumer Installation and event-specific non-widening authorization

findings.summary: Derive Agent Runner qualification from an all-passed exact test set and approved canary.
findings.failure_scenario: A failed or blocked conformance case is hidden behind green summary counters, or a passing qualification has no approved canary evidence.
findings.impact: An unsafe Agent Runner adapter could otherwise become launch-eligible.
findings.minimum_fix: Implemented all-passed schema constraints and semantic derivation of unique cases and summary counts, plus an approved passing canary with evidence for launch eligibility.
findings.architecture_boundary: replaceable Agent Runner qualification and launch authority

findings.summary: Bind provider status to the exact migration chain and status-specific evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: A projection substitutes another run or candidate, or reports retired using merge-only evidence.
findings.impact: Provider-visible rollout state could otherwise overstate or cross-contaminate consumer progress.
findings.minimum_fix: Implemented exact run, installation, authorization, plan, candidate, verification, and delivery binding rules with deterministic invalidation and a distinct retirement_confirmation requirement.

findings.summary: Validate provider-visible payloads through a strict typed fail-closed vocabulary.
findings.failure_scenario: Raw consumer data or a credential is hidden under an innocuous arbitrary or nested field and sent to the API Provider.
findings.impact: Consumer-private source, prompts, traces, sessions, or credentials could otherwise cross the provider boundary.
findings.minimum_fix: Implemented strict typed decoding with unknown-field rejection, fixed consented vocabulary, nested structural validation, privacy constants, and adversarial secret or private-material tests.
findings.architecture_boundary: redaction before persistence and API Provider disclosure

findings.summary: Bind trusted validation evidence to the canonical candidate and exact command outputs.
findings.failure_scenario: Free-text or stale validation claims are copied forward after candidate or command output changes.
findings.impact: High-risk promotion could otherwise become false-green without cryptographic reconciliation.
findings.minimum_fix: The trusted runner now emits one validation_run_id, the canonical base-plus-candidate binding, ordered command results, per-command runner identity and timestamps, and SHA-256-bound markers and stdout or stderr logs; this review independently recomputed every binding.
findings.architecture_boundary: Factory validation, review, and promotion evidence

findings.summary: Complete sandbox isolation binding before later runtimes can consume the manifest.
findings.failure_scenario: A schema-valid sandbox profile can set its neutral home or temp root to the runtime-resolved host home or an OS credential-store path because only mount sources are compared with the host boundary. Its single sandbox credential grant may also carry extra scope IDs, and duplicate network or credential grant IDs remain ambiguous because uniqueness is checked only over complete JSON objects. The semantic boundary omits sandbox resource quotas, so profile and manifest isolation quotas can disagree. Separately, workflow_verified_replay or workflow_verified_mock returns before comparing exact-head outcome evidence with the candidate head; only workflow_verified_sandbox performs that comparison.
findings.impact: A later M7 or M8 runtime could accept a persisted contract that exposes host state, widens credential scope, resolves an ambiguous grant, weakens sandbox resource limits, or reports a stale workflow outcome as exact-head verified. These are fail-open gaps on the host-isolation and proof-integrity boundaries.
findings.minimum_fix: Implemented runtime-host-bound neutral-root overlap rejection, exact one-profile sandbox credential scope, globally unique network and credential grant IDs, positive semantic resource-quota validation, current-candidate binding for every observed verification item, exact-head outcome requirements for replay and mock verification, and rejection of sandbox-profile bindings on non-sandbox evidence.
findings.architecture_boundary: host-enforced command and credential-bearing sandbox isolation

findings.summary: Route persisted Consumer Installation and Event Authorization authority through canonical schemas and one production non-widening entry point.
findings.failure_scenario: A runtime decodes a flattened bespoke Installation or AuthorizationSnapshot, or invokes snapshot validation directly, without validating the canonical persisted schemas and independently expected artifact and policy bindings.
findings.impact: Schema-valid consumer authority, event identity, repository scope, policy digests, budgets, or provider-reporting consent could otherwise be substituted or widened before a side-effecting runtime consumes them.
findings.minimum_fix: Implemented embedded canonical schema validation, strict typed decoding with unknown-field and trailing-JSON rejection, non-widening conversion, independently supplied expected bindings, and one exported persisted-artifact snapshot entry point while keeping direct snapshot validation package-private.
findings.architecture_boundary: persisted Consumer Installation and event-specific execution authority

findings.summary: Emit only the declared and consented provider projection instead of returning the complete control artifact.
findings.failure_scenario: A validation-only API succeeds and a caller serializes the original complete provider-status artifact, including consumer-private consent, privacy, interpretation, and integrity-control metadata or fields outside the external consent ceiling.
findings.impact: The API Provider could receive more data than the exact event-bound field declaration and consumer consent allow.
findings.minimum_fix: Replaced the validation-only return with BuildProviderPayload, which validates the complete typed artifact, intersects declared fields with any external consent ceiling, serializes a new exact-field ProviderPayload, and rejects structural/control metadata, unknown fields, duplicate or widening consent, and private material.

findings.summary: Regenerate the complete active controls with the aligned Lumyn profile, exact M2 security review, and lifecycle-pending state.
findings.failure_scenario: Stale compiled controls retain the superseded profile incompatibility or a generic review lens, or overstate M2 acceptance closure despite pending CI, latest-head review, merge, post-merge, and item-level lifecycle evidence.
findings.impact: Planning, review, dispatch, or closure could follow a different contract from the current product and Factory profile.
findings.minimum_fix: Regenerated all active compiled artifacts to the exact aligned profile version, preserved factoryd pause and release freeze, set M2 review_type to security with independent-or-human review, and kept M2 implementation locally complete but lifecycle and acceptance closure pending.
findings.architecture_boundary: compiled Factory planning, review routing, runtime authority, and acceptance closure

findings.summary: Make repo-pack validation reject M2 risk-class and security-review routing drift.
findings.failure_scenario: Before repair, an in-memory mutation could downgrade M2 risk_class from high to medium, change either the M2 inherited or global required review_type from security to code, or change the declared reviewer class while validate_loaded still returned success.
findings.impact: A later edit can silently weaken the required high-risk security review while make test-contracts and the repo-pack gate remain false-green, allowing commit-push to accept a less stringent review declaration.
findings.minimum_fix: Implemented exact risk-class enforcement for all 12 tasks, exact per-task review-type enforcement, independent-or-human reviewer enforcement, the global security review and exact task-lens source checks, and negative self-tests for M2 risk, review-type, and reviewer-class downgrades plus global routing downgrades.
findings.architecture_boundary: executable Factory risk classification and security-review routing

residual_risks: M2 is contract-only; provider fetch, repository analysis, Agent Runner launch, credential issuance, verification, GitHub delivery, and provider reporting runtime behavior remain unproven until their later milestones produce direct evidence.

The current compiled artifacts and repo-pack validator enforce the exact task risk classes, task-specific review lenses, independent-or-human reviewer class, global security lens, and aligned profile; factoryd remains explicitly unqualified and paused.
Remote CI and CodeQL, current-head passive Codex review, PR lifecycle evidence, merge, and post-main monitoring remain pending lifecycle gates and are not granted by this review.

state_impact: M2 introduces persisted authority, Agent Runner qualification, evidence, verification, provider-reporting, and compiled review-routing contracts for later runtimes; the executable repo-pack gate now binds the exact task risk and review policy.
source_of_truth_changes: The v3 schemas and semantic validators are the M2 product-contract source of truth, while the active compiled control set plus repo-pack validator are the review-routing and lifecycle source of truth.
feedback_plan: Keep the risk and review-route downgrade mutations in the repo-pack self-test, and keep future runtime milestones exercising product contracts at the authoritative boundary and feeding escaped false-green paths back into adversarial fixtures and security review.
blast_radius: The contracts affect every later provider-event, repository-command, Agent Runner, verification, live-sandbox, delivery, and provider-reporting milestone; exact per-task risk and review checks now prevent those later tasks from silently inheriting weaker review policy, while their product runtimes remain unimplemented.
rollback_or_deletion_test: Isolation mutations remain rejected; independent in-memory mutations of all 12 task risk classes, M2 and M2.5 review lenses, reviewer classes, the global security lens, and the lens source are rejected; and candidate, marker, and raw-log digests reconcile exactly.
systems_questions.system_model_summary: All 11 findings are independently resolved. The exact 105-path candidate, four markers, and every raw log bind to the trusted passing validation run; focused product-security tests and 18 adversarial risk or review-route downgrades pass fail-closed verification. Security review is approved and ready for PR, while remote CI, current-head passive review, merge, post-merge monitoring, and later runtime proof remain pending lifecycle work.
